packs.title: Harbor, houses and the wider city
packs.promise: Enter museums, attend a performance and follow public trails across Portsmouth.

q.s: Attend a complete public performance or film, then make an original response.
st: Choose a suitable actual event and obtain its ticket before planning the outing. Follow its arrival, age and admission terms.
Watch or listen to the full event with your phone put away. Notice an unresolved question, change of mood or relationship between parts.
After leaving, create a short original scene, sound description or sketch responding to that question. Describe your own idea without reproducing a song, film frame or performer’s words.

q.s: Browse the operating farmers market and make a meal plan from today’s actual offerings.
st: Visit while the market is operating and browse without blocking stalls or customers.
Choose a small set of currently offered ingredients that could form a meal. Read available product information and use prices only if actually displayed.
Write your meal plan and explain one substitution you would make if a chosen ingredient sold out. Identify which ingredients you actually saw.

q.s: Take an open public trail and compare the conditions at a habitat transition.
st: Start at the actual public trail approach and follow an open signed route. Note your turn-around point before continuing.
At a visible transition, compare two conditions you can observe safely from the path, such as light, wind exposure or ground cover. Keep an observation distinct from a guess.
On returning, make a prediction about how one condition could affect the plants there and describe what further observation would test it.

packs.title: Market Square to the island in two afternoons
packs.promise: Connect public rooms, independent shops, gardens and a café through downtown walks.

q.s: Explore the free grounds and design a small entrance sequence of your own.
st: Walk the actual open grounds paths and notice how an entrance, arbor or change in enclosure shapes your movement.
Choose one principle that creates a transition, such as narrowing then opening, shade then light or a pause before a turn. Describe its actual source in the grounds.
Design an original entrance sequence for a small place of your choosing. Explain the change in pace you want rather than copying the garden layout.

q.t: A plan for a waterfront garden
q.s: Walk the public garden paths and make a design with room for changing seasons.
st: Explore open garden paths and choose a relationship you can actually observe between a path, planted height, shade or open space.
Choose two practical constraints for your own small garden, including room for seasonal change.
Make an original plan and explain how the observed relationship helped solve one constraint. Your plan need not reproduce any planting or artwork.

q.s: Visit the café and build a short sensory sequence from an actual food choice.
st: Choose an actually available food item after checking ingredients and suitability with the café if needed. Pay its actual price and follow service instructions.
Once safely seated or stopped where permitted, notice three moments: first appearance, first bite and a change as you continue. Do not photograph or record other customers.
Write a short original sequence that conveys those changes without giving it an invented historical story or a predetermined positive review.
